item.title: Recruiting for a Community Survey
item.description: Evaluate who takes part in a fictional local survey about park hours. Distinguish who can be selected, who participates or drops out, and how the answers themselves are produced.

children.definition: A list or other operational record of the units from which a sample is drawn.
children.example: The team used the town’s household register as its sampling frame and randomly selected 300 households for the park-hours survey.
children.translation_uz: tanlanma tuzish uchun asos boʻladigan roʻyxat yoki reyestr
collocations: check the sampling frame for duplicates

children.definition: The failure to obtain a usable questionnaire from a person or household selected for a survey.
children.example: The team recorded unit nonresponse when a selected household returned no questionnaire by the closing date.
children.translation_ru: отсутствие пригодной для обработки анкеты от единицы выборки
children.translation_uz: tanlanmaga kiritilgan shaxs yoki xonadondan foydalanishga yaroqli anketa olinmasligi

children.definition: The time, effort or inconvenience a person faces when providing the information a survey requests.
children.example: To reduce respondent burden, the park survey asked residents which evenings they would use the park instead of asking them to reconstruct a month of visits.
children.translation_uz: soʻrovga javob berish uchun sarflanadigan vaqt va kuch hamda bu bilan bogʻliq noqulayliklar

children.definition: A person or organization that controls whether researchers can contact a group.
children.example: The housing association acted as a gatekeeper because only it could send the survey invitation to residents on its mailing list.
children.translation_ru: лицо или организация, от которых зависит доступ исследователей к группе людей
children.translation_uz: tadqiqotchilarning muayyan guruh bilan bogʻlanishiga ruxsat beradigan shaxs yoki tashkilot

children.definition: A means of delivering an invitation to potential participants in a study or survey.
children.example: The organisers used postal invitations as a recruitment channel for the park-hours survey, with a web link and a phone number for replying.

children.definition: A situation in which a group makes up a smaller share of the people surveyed than it does of the population the survey is intended to describe.
children.example: To check for underrepresentation of adults aged 18 to 24, the team compared their share of park-hours survey respondents with their share of the district’s adult population.
children.translation_uz: guruhning soʻrov ishtirokchilari orasidagi ulushi soʻrov qamrab olishi kerak boʻlgan aholi orasidagi ulushidan kichik boʻlishi

children.definition: A gap in the group a survey can reach because some members of its target population are left out of the sampling frame.
children.example: The team identified undercoverage when it found that newly converted flats were missing from its household register.
children.translation_uz: tanlash uchun ishlatiladigan roʻyxat maqsadli aholining bir qismini qamrab olmasligi

children.definition: A message sent after an initial survey invitation to prompt the recipient to complete the questionnaire.
children.example: A week after the initial park-hours invitation, the team sent a reminder to households that had yet to reply.

children.definition: An account a participant gives of their own behaviour, circumstances or experiences.
children.example: The survey used each resident’s self-report of their visits after 7 p.m. to estimate how often that resident had used the park in the evening.

children.definition: A person who provides survey information on behalf of the individual selected to participate.
children.example: With her father’s agreement, a daughter acted as his proxy respondent and reported how often he visited the park after dinner.
children.translation_ru: респондент, который отвечает на вопросы опроса вместо отобранного участника и сообщает сведения о нём
children.translation_uz: boshqa kishi nomidan javob beruvchi respondent
collocations: accept answers from a proxy respondent

children.definition: A difference in survey results that arises because the way people enter the study favours people whose characteristics or views are relevant to what is being measured.
children.example: The team considered a possible selection effect when people recruited at the park after 7 p.m. were more likely to favour later closing than people recruited through a household mailing.
children.translation_uz: ishtirokchilarning tadqiqotga qanday jalb etilgani natijalarga koʻrsatadigan taʼsir

children.definition: A recurring tendency for participants’ answers to depart from what actually happened in a consistent way.
children.example: If residents regularly counted walks past the park as visits, this systematic misreporting would inflate the survey’s estimate of park use.

children.definition: The loss of participants between rounds of a study after they have already taken part.
children.example: The team measured attrition by checking how many residents who completed the first park-hours questionnaire failed to take part in the second round.

children.definition: A survey answer processed so that the person who gave it can no longer reasonably be identified, either from the answer itself or by linking it to other information.
children.example: The report quoted an anonymized response about earlier park opening after the team removed the resident’s identifying details and checked the remaining wording for clues to their identity.
children.translation_uz: kim berganini aniqlab boʻlmaydigan shaklga keltirilgan javob
